messages:
alex: Heads-up: after last night's driver rollout (515.xx -> 530.xx) we're seeing Hopper (H100) canary failures in eu-west2. SM90 PTX kernels keep falling back or failing to load.
ops-bot: deploy: driver-rollout-eu-west2 started by infra-cd @ 1976540800 :rocket:
maria: Seeing kernel link errors in the node logs, GPU pods OOM'ing during kernel JIT. Example from node-gn-03: `ptx_compiler: link failed: invalid PTX version or unsupported instruction`
ranjit: Can you paste the exact dmesg / nvidia logs? Is this only SM90 models or also older SM80?
alex: Only SM90 models so far (hopper variants). SM80 jobs look fine. dmesg snippet: ```
[ 2345.678901] nvidia: ptx: failed to load ptx, signature mismatch
[ 2345.678904] nvidia: kernel compilation error: unsupported PTX ISA 7.0 for current driver
```
jen: Important: we have two Dedicated clusters in eu-west2 running prod queues. If this spreads we hit SLA risk. What was the driver minimum we set? I thought runtime enforces 525+ for SM90?
thomas: We documented driver minimum 530 for the new runtime, but the CUDA toolchain used for JIT compiled kernels in our images expects 525-compatible PTX. So mismatch. Looks like the driver PR changed PTX validation strictness.
maria: Quick mitigation: taint the canary node pool and drain Hopper workloads, switch them to fallback pool (SM80/other regions). That buys time but capacity is tight.
ranjit: Agreed, but draining will cause scaling in other regions -> cross-region egress and cost spike. Estimated extra reserved-hours ~ 40 GPU-hours if we keep it for 6h.
alex: Plan proposal: 1) immediately cordon/taint affected canary pools in eu-west2, 2) patch runtime to force use of cubin (precompiled kernels) for SM90 in rollout, 3) roll back driver to 525 on canary until we validate new toolchain.
jen: If we roll back node driver images we need to coordinate with infra-ci-bot to avoid auto-upgrade. infra-ci-bot: please halt auto-upgrades for eu-west2 canaries.
infra-ci-bot: auto-upgrades: paused for cluster eu-west2-canary by request of jen at 1976543220
thomas: The precompiled cubin approach reduces JIT issues but will likely increase image size and complicate variant builds. Can we do a targeted fallback only for the problematic model families?
maria: Yes, runtime supports model routing. We can add a per-model annotation to prefer cubin for models tagged `hopper-sm90` — quick config change on the routing layer.
ranjit: Diagnostic ask: collect `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log`, `dmesg`, and `kubectl describe pod` for 3 failed pods and upload to #eng-infra-artifacts. I captured one to s3://redwood-diagnostics/1976543210/node-gn-03.log
alex: Thanks. I'll start the cordon + routing config change now and post updates. If anyone notices failures in other regions ping me @alex immediately. :warning:
jen: After we stabilize, we should add an automated compatibility test in our canary gate that runs a small SM90 JIT workload to detect PTX/driver strictness changes before rollout.
thomas: Agree — add to postmortem and make it a hard gate. Also open ticket to upstream driver vendor with reproducer and request clarification on PTX validation changes.
alex: Update 1976543285: cordon + taint done on eu-west2 canary pool (nodes 01-04). Routing annotation applied for `hopper-sm90` -> `prefer-cubin`. Monitoring shows failed job rate down 90%. Leaving this thread open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
